headline: The overnight chip sell-off held into Europe, and a strong German survey couldn't turn it
tone: Still risk-off at midday: Europe picked up Asia's AI-chip selling rather than shrugging it off, and a Deutsche Bank scandal added a bank-specific hit before Nvidia reports after the US close.
body: The overnight story held, it didn't flip. Europe's chip names took the US licensing rule on rented AI computing the same way Asia did: ASML lost about 3% and STMicro 2.5%, and Reuters had European tech down about 2% as a sector. The worry is a smaller future market for AI hardware, not this quarter's sales.

The morning's one data point was good news the market ignored. Germany's ZEW expectations index jumped to 35.6 from 28.1, well above the 28.3 Reuters poll, with ZEW citing rising factory orders and cheaper oil. It did nothing for stocks or the euro, which stays near its lowest since April 2025: with a December ECB hike already priced, better German data mainly backs that hike.

Deutsche Bank fell about 6% after leaked internal documents tied it to Russian oligarchs and Jeffrey Epstein, which the FT says involved nearly $600 million of suspicious payments. That is a compliance story, not a credit one, but it put a large bank among the day's biggest fallers alongside tech.

The miners are where the money is leaving fastest, as copper sits near a four-month low on the same AI-capex doubts. Oil is still not trading the Gulf attacks; returning Middle East exports and the surplus outweigh them. What would change the tone: Nvidia guidance showing overseas data-centre demand survives the new rule, or a strong US retail sales print this afternoon. Anthropic's listing on Thursday is the next test of appetite for AI.

views.text: Priced in for midday: caution into Nvidia, with Europe's recent rotation out of US tech not protecting it from chip and bank selling. A soft Nvidia guide would hit chip equipment and the miners again; a clean beat would likely bring the morning's losers back first.

A strong ZEW only firms the case for the December ECB hike that is already priced, so it leaves rates and the euro mostly unchanged. US retail sales this afternoon matter more for the dollar and Fed hike bets.
